Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates dextrocardia (heart apex pointing to the right) and a left-sided horizontal fissure, which are radiographic signs of situs inversus. This finding, combined with the clinical history of sinusitis and recurrent respiratory infections (suggesting bronchiectasis/primary ciliary dyskinesia), supports the diagnosis of Kartagener syndrome.
